source.name: Global Soil Partnership endorses guidelines on sustainable soil management
source.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

cadence: Annual FAO Global Soil Partnership assessment review.
provenance: Official FAO Global Soil Partnership summary of global annual arable-soil erosion and associated agricultural-production loss. Source units and annual recurrence are retained.
uncertainty: The summary provides point estimates without observation-level uncertainty. Global aggregation combines heterogeneous climates, soils, land uses and methods; erosion, deposition and soil formation vary. Agricultural-production loss depends on valuation and attribution assumptions.
failure_behavior: Retain the last reviewed assessment and mark stale. Reject changed units, annualization or arable-land boundaries. Never infer remaining topsoil stock, distribute a global estimate uniformly, fill missing uncertainty with zero, or treat the point estimate as a globally comparable acceleration trend.

assessment.source_locator: FAO newsroom statement: globally 75 billion tonnes of soil are lost from arable land each year and an estimated US$400 billion in agricultural production is lost.
assessment.measurement_boundary: Annual global burden estimate, not current acceleration, net soil balance, remaining soil depth or a country panel.
